construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Depth meeting depth cross-polarity — intelligence competing with intelligence
candidates.k2_overview: Your Water moves as the Rival: current that races current. You compete the way tides do, quietly, continuously, gaining by inches that look like accidents. Shared flows suit you: pooled funds, joint journeys, split winnings. Just remember that merged water is hard to unmix. Mark what is yours before the confluence.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy ebbs and floods: read your own tide chart and schedule accordingly.

k2_domain_readings.Rivalry: Your rivalries run underwater: unspoken races, silent measurements, positions gained without visible waves. Surface one or two. A named, laughing rivalry refreshes you more than ten secret ones.
k2_domain_readings.Shared stakes: Money and effort pool around you like watersheds: group funds, family flows, blended accounts. You track it all mentally and forgive it all eventually. Put banks around what must not flood away.
k2_domain_readings.Boldness: Your daring is fluid: risks taken by drift and momentum more than announcement. It carries you far. Just check occasionally that the current you are riding is one you chose.

angles.drive: A race gets all of you moving. You run on a small supply of Water, and chasing a real person refills it better than following a plan. When you name one race a season out loud, you come out of it fed rather than spent.
angles.cost_self: You feel most alive inside a race. You have little Water, and you race more than you rest and spend what the quiet weeks put back. Rest between races as hard as you run them, and you bring full stamina to the next one.
angles.cost_others: Every race you love needs someone else in it. You make a rival of a peer rather than ask them first, and they run a race they never chose. If you tell them the race is on, you run it together instead of alone.

angles.drive: Jumping in first is how you learn what a thing is like. Water is short in you, and being inside a decision suits you better than planning beside it. If you jump in where stakes are shared, you pay half of the first mistake.
angles.cost_self: Going first is where your boldness lives. Little Water backs you, and you jump in ahead of reading the plan, while early mistakes come out of your savings. When you read the plan first every third time, you hold on to more of your money.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you go first, you pull your partner in after you. You decide for both ahead of asking, and you take the risk in their name too. If you ask before you jump, you go in side by side.

angles.drive: Going all in together is the only way you go in. Shared stakes feel more real to you than a safe share kept back, so you pool money and effort. When you pick people who count as carefully as you trust, all in pays off.
angles.cost_self: Inside a shared stake, you feel your bravest. A pooled stake feels like company, and all in feels better to you than holding some back. If you keep one share out of every pool, you only ever lose what you can afford.
angles.cost_others: All in together means you take someone with you every time. You put the shared stake ahead of asking whose it was, and a partner carries losses they never signed for. You keep a partner past the risk by agreeing the shares before it.

angles.drive: Racing in secret keeps the race one you cannot lose. Water builds up in you unseen, so you measure a friend quietly rather than name the race. With the race never named, you run it alone and finish it alone.
angles.cost_self: Secret racing keeps you safe while you race. Water gathers in you with nowhere to go, and you spend it on quiet races rather than on one open try. You never get the win said out loud.
angles.cost_others: In secret, you make a friend a rival without asking them. You keep the race hidden rather than risk losing it in the open. You take away their chance to answer, or to race you openly.

angles.drive: Spending shared money comes easier to you than spending your own. Shared money feels like courage, and you dip into it ahead of asking who put what in. You run the pool down faster than agreed, and slowing it is yours to do.
angles.cost_self: Spending from the shared pot is the easiest money there is. More Water moves through you than you keep, so you pay for everyone's good time ahead of your savings. You come out with the least from a pot you paid the most into.
angles.cost_others: Each time you spend what was pooled, you spend someone else's decision. You move the money rather than ask, and you leave a partner a smaller share than they put in. You want everyone looked after, and some of that comes out of their share.

angles.drive: Never enough is the rule under everything you win. Water keeps rising in you and never lands, and you want the next prize more than the one in hand. You never named a finish line, so you never get to cross one.
angles.cost_self: Never having enough keeps you bold after the boldness has paid. Water runs over in you, and you spend the win on the next race rather than bank it. You end each year with more wins than savings.
angles.cost_others: Whenever enough is not enough, you keep your partners running past their finish. You push for the next round ahead of asking, and they put in more than they meant. You call it done, and letting them stop counts as a win too.

edge.lead: Water runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the money you chase harder once someone else wants it, the dare your friends already know you will take, and the new way through you find when the old one closes.
